comparison: Perfect agreement on touch dome emergence at E16.5 and Merkel cell spatiotemporal dynamics (C1, C22-C29, C88-C93). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with no challenges to the temporal characterization or quantification.

Disagreement on BMP4-expressing dermal cells (C30-C32, C94-C97). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for CFPhigh cell clustering and correlation with touch dome emergence. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning cell identity confirmation and specificity of noggin manipulation targeting these cells.

Agreement on BMP signaling temporal requirements (C2, C3, C36, C70-C72, C98-C99). Both find evidence SUPPORTED for differential effects of E14.5 vs E17.5 noggin induction. Peer review acknowledges discrete BMP-expressing mesenchymal population contribution despite questioning manipulation specificity.

Disagreement on innervation temporal progression (C37-C40, C103-C104). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with well-documented progression from E15.5 to P21. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning evidence for exuberant sprouting at E18.5 and requesting additional quantification.

Perfect agreement on two distinct neuronal populations (C4-C5, C41-C51, C105-C107, C109). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly affirms the novel identification of TrkC-negative NFH-positive transient population distinct from TrkC-positive Merkel cell-associated terminals.

Agreement on K17-positive keratinocyte necessity for innervation (C6-C7, C52-C55, C100-C101). Both find SUPPORTED based on K17 ablation experiments showing dramatic reduction in terminal endings. Peer review explicitly affirms necessity claim.

Disagreement on K17-positive keratinocyte sufficiency (C56-C59, C102). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on Shh overexpression expanding K17 cells and increasing innervation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning why Merkel cells didn't increase and noting insufficient quantification with data relegated to supplementary material.

Agreement on Merkel cell dispensability for embryonic innervation (C60-C61, C81). Both find SUPPORTED based on Atoh1 knockout data. Peer review explicitly affirms the study builds on previous work demonstrating Merkel cells are dispensable for sensory terminal recruitment.

Both address Merkel cell role in postnatal refinement (C82). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as inference from absence of embryonic effects plus literature, noting current study doesn't directly test postnatal refinement. Peer review includes C82 in SUPPORTED evaluation but focuses on embryonic dispensability rather than postnatal role.

Agreement on integrative model (C62, C65). Both find the conceptual framework SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C62 is appropriately labeled as proposed model/speculation. Peer review describes work as 'thoughtfully discussed' and 'significant contribution,' requesting improved presentation but not challenging conclusions.

Agreement on K17 keratinocyte necessity and sufficiency conclusion (C84). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by integrating embryonic experiments with adult maintenance literature. Peer review explicitly states study 'establishes the necessity and sufficiency of K17 expressing epithelial cells for touch dome innervation.'

OpenEval evaluated background knowledge and prior work claims (C8-C21, C66-C69, C73-C80, C83, C85-C87, C96, C108) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual/literature claims.
